headline: Calf improving but still felt, and HRV baseline has slid 36→32 with little load behind it; trim 16–22 Nov to ~38 km and hold the November step.
review_md:
# Weekly review — Sunday 15 November 2026

Shep — the calf is better than last week but not yet clear, and the recovery numbers have slid for the first time since the return. Adjust: the 16–22 Nov week comes down, and the November step waits.

## The week (9–15 Nov)

Planned about 36 km. Done: **30.2 km over four runs** — 5.2 (Tue), 7.0 (Wed), 8.0 treadmill (Fri), 10.0 (Sat) — plus bike, ski erg and isometrics Monday and rest Thursday. All easy, HR 123–143, RPE 1, achilles 0 every day. Saturday was 4 km over the 6 km prescribed; I said last night why I'd rather you hadn't, and I'm not repeating it. Sunday is rest/bike, as planned.

## Calf

Felt on three of four runs: end of Wed's, the treadmill on Fri, the start of Sat's (1/10, faded to nothing). Fading as you warm is the benign pattern, the opposite of 1 Nov, and nothing built or lingered. But "tiny" has now repeated, so this is not yet a week of nothing felt. **Tuesday 17 Nov is the test**; the log line I need is when you noticed it and whether it faded or built. If it is felt a fourth time, that is the physio call.

## Recovery — the part that has changed

- HRV 7-day baseline: 36 on 8 Nov → **32 today**, three weeks flat before that. Nights this week: 32, 32, 37, **28**, 33, 31, 32.
- RHR: 46–48 most days, **52 on Thu 12 Nov** (HRV 28, sleep score 69), then 49, 51, 48.
- Flagged 12 Nov, no confounder in the notes. Principle 3 allows leaving a single flat morning alone, but the baseline has now slid for a week, and the limit applies: a confounder excuses a morning, not a trend.
- What makes it odd: load is tiny. ACWR 0.7–0.9, 30 km a week, all at RPE 1. This is not a training-load dip, and I will not blame the calf runs for it. Sleep is fine (8.6–9.8 h, scores 81–86, which is more sleep than usual). Garmin reads "strained", which I treat as a nudge, not evidence.
- Unexplained HRV slide with little load behind it is also what an approaching illness looks like before it is felt. Neck check: any chest symptoms, temperature or aches, no hard session. Nothing in your notes suggests it, so this is a watch, not a finding. If you know something I don't (work, stress, alcohol), put it in the log and I'll read it that way.

## Efficiency and base

Easy runs 5:00/km at HR ~136 for the week, efficiency 1.48, in line with prior weeks. Treadmill pace was wrong on the watch (belt 6:00/km); ignore it for pace trends. Nothing to read into one clean week.

## Load check

`volume_target.json` marks 23–29 Nov `under` (56 vs curve 67.9), and 30 Nov unplanned. I'm **not** raising them, and say why: two gates hold — the calf note of 11 Nov (and three more since) and two unexplained readiness flags in seven days. You are also about 10 days behind the Nov shape, which the March peak can absorb at under 2 km/week. The agreed rule is that gates stop the push, not that the curve is abandoned.

16–22 Nov was planned at 58 km against a cap of 37.8 off a 30 km week; that is `over` and gets cut. The cut is mild, and it shifts the long run down, since volume is negotiable and the leg sessions are not.

## Proposal (three weeks)

- **16–22 Nov: ~38 km.** Tue 10 (the test), Wed 6, Thu 8, Fri rest, Sat 6, Sun 8 easy (not 16). Gym legs Wed or Thu. No strides.
- **23–29 Nov, provisional: ~44 km** (was 56). Long 12. Strides return Wed only if both calf and HRV have been quiet.
- **30 Nov–6 Dec, provisional: ~52 km.** Long 16. Tempo not before the week after, and not in a week volume is also rising.

If Tuesday is silent and HRV baseline is back to 35+ by the Wednesday after, the next review lifts toward the curve. If either isn't, it holds again. This is slower than the curve, and cheap: you have five months to the marathon and the climb to 95–100 needs only ~2 km a week.

## Admin

Wokingham Half (21 Feb) entry still to make; Fission 20 opens 1 Jan.

## Recommendation: adjust

Cut 16–22 Nov to ~38 km, hold the November step until the calf is silent and HRV has recovered.

conversation.athlete_thoughts: I acknowledge the HRV drop but I'm doing hardly anything and feel totally fine and have done so for weeks.  If the calf was fine I'd be carrying on as normal. Once calf is ok the HRV will NOT be slowing my progress because it's down when I'm feeling totally fine
conversation.coach_reply:
Shep — you're right on the HRV, and I'm taking it out as a brake.

You feel fine, you have no symptoms, and the load is about as low as it gets (ACWR 0.7–0.9, all RPE 1). Under your 4 Oct instruction that is yours to overrule, so I've done it. One sentence of risk, then I drop it: an unexplained HRV slide with no load behind it is also what illness looks like before it's felt, so the neck check still applies (chest symptoms, temperature or aches mean no hard session). I'm not treating it as a limit on the November build.

But it wasn't the main reason for the cut, so that part doesn't move. 16–22 Nov stays at ~38 km because the ramp cap off a 30 km week is 37.8, and because the calf has been felt on three of four runs. "Tiny, faded as I warmed" is the benign pattern, but it hasn't yet been a week of nothing. You said yourself that if the calf were fine you'd carry on as normal. That is the gate, and Tuesday's 10 km is the test.

What changes is the weeks after, provisionally: 23–29 Nov to 47 km (was 44) and 30 Nov–6 Dec to 56 km (was 52), the long run building to 16. That's the ramp cap, not the curve, which I still won't chase while the calf is unsettled. If Tuesday is silent and the next week stays silent, the following review moves toward the curve. If the calf is felt a fourth time, it's the physio call, not a debate about numbers. The revised proposal is on the dashboard for you to approve.

Shep — nothing to answer here: your 15 Nov approval came with no question, and the 18 Nov hold-and-bike proposal is already approved and applied (9:05 today).

The plan as it now stands: no running until the calf is 0/10 (not 1) on walking, stairs, single-leg raises and hops for three days and your physio has cleared it; bike and her calf loading meanwhile; then run-walk, gated each time on 0/10 during and the next morning. If you meant to say something with that submission, send it again and I'll pick it up.
